issues.body: In `ChangeRelay::pump`, a `SinkError::Permanent` returned by `deliver` is only saved in `failure`; `self.fail(seq, e)` is deferred until after `self.sink.flush()` and `write_cursor(...)`. If flush returns an error, that error returns first and the earlier permanent refusal never reaches `fail`. Likewise, when an accepted prefix exists, a cursor-write failure returns before `fail`. In both cases `self.poisoned` remains unset, so a later `pump` can call the sink again despite the public promise that a permanent refusal poisons the live relay and makes every subsequent pump fail closed.
issues.fix_hint: Poison the relay immediately when `deliver` returns `SinkError::Permanent`, before any fallible flush or cursor bookkeeping, while retaining the refusal to return after safely handling any accepted prefix. Add real-path tests for an accepted prefix followed by a permanent refusal where (1) the subsequent flush fails retryably and (2) cursor persistence fails; in both cases assert `is_poisoned()` and assert that the next `pump` returns `RelayError::Poisoned` without another delivery attempt.
issues.title: Permanent delivery refusal can still be masked without poisoning

verdict.summary: Round 5 is stagnant: the prior major fail-closed finding remains. A permanent delivery refusal is stored in `failure`, but the relay is not poisoned until after the fallible sink flush and cursor persistence steps. Consequently, a later flush or cursor error can mask the permanent refusal and leave the live relay able to deliver again. The tests still cover only the successful post-refusal flush/cursor path, not either masking path required to establish the documented contract.
